chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from al-Halabi, that he asked him about a person in ihram who trimmed his fingernails, he said:
Upon him is a mud for each finger. If he trimmed all ten of them, then upon him is the blood of a sheep.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A person in the state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific measure of food (approx. 0.75 kg)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for trimming fingernails while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar establishes the graduated fidya for trimming fingernails during ihram, distinguishing between the minor expiation of a mud of food for a single nail and the major expiation of a sheep for all ten. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise proportional liability (kaffarah) based on the extent of the violation, as recorded by Shaykh al-Tusi in his compilation of practical legal rulings.
